result.headline: No control fault found; attitude tracks setpoints, but yaw error is large and airspeed and yaw-rate channels are dead.
result.explanation: Roll, pitch and actuator steps follow commanded manoeuvres and tracking errors stay small. Yaw error is large all flight, and airspeed and yaw rate never change, which points at sensor or estimator channels rather than a control event.

evidence.quote: TRACKING control.attitude_setpoint[yaw] vs vehicle.attitude[yaw]: steady lag 2.473 s removed (a constant lag is this recording's normal, not a fault); typical |error| 40.112 deg, worst 144.961 at t=0 s; 1 window(s) above 120.335
evidence.shows: Yaw error is large through the whole flight (about 32-44 deg per stretch after the start). It is not an onset fault.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT vehicle.airspeed = 0 for the whole recording (411 samples)
evidence.shows: The airspeed channel never changes while the aircraft moves at 16-19 m/s, so it is dead or not populated.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT vehicle.yaw_rate[yaw] = 0 for the whole recording (139 samples)
evidence.shows: The yaw-rate channel is also constant for the whole recording.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.163 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A start-up sensor-health error is consistent with the dead sensor channels. It is a start-up line, so no case is built on it alone.

evidence.quote: CHANGE control.attitude_setpoint[roll] at t=10.187 s: 34.735 -> 7.58 deg (step -27.155, 1357.7x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The large roll steps are commanded in the setpoint. Measured roll follows with a lag, so these are manoeuvres.

checked.check: Read the events and all CHANGE, SHIFT and TRACKING lines
checked.result: Only two start-up events (low voltage warning, sensor health error) and no mode changes. The tracking lines show typical errors of 1.7 deg (pitch) and 2.3 deg (roll).

checked.check: Sequence of departures from baseline, t=5-13 s
checked.result: Velocity, yaw setpoint and roll setpoint left baseline first. The actuator steps at 9.722 s came after those and before the roll step in the attitude estimate at 10.389 s.

checked.check: Compare before and after t=9.722 s (the 3-channel actuator step)
checked.result: Nothing froze. Roll setpoint moved 44.49 to 12.91 deg and measured roll moved 46.296 to 17.021 deg. Tracking error ratios were 1.5-1.69 and no output froze, as expected for a commanded roll-out.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[roll] at t=10.743 s: 42.148 -> 17.021 deg (step -25.127, 6x its usual variation)
effects.why: This is the measured response to the commanded roll-setpoint step at 10.187 s, not an independent fault.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.velocity[x] changed level for good at t=5.865 s: median 16.07 before, -7.74 after m/s (4.2x its variation before)
effects.why: The velocity sign flips come with heading changes during the manoeuvres and are not tied to any fault onset.

next_action.action: Check airspeed sensor and yaw/compass calibration and logging configuration for flight-16.
next_action.why: Settles whether the constant airspeed and yaw-rate channels and the large yaw error are a logging or sensor-configuration issue rather than a flight fault.
how: Check whether a pitot or airspeed sensor is fitted, enabled and calibrated
Check the compass and yaw calibration status and the heading reference convention (wrap or offset)
Confirm the log mapping for yaw_rate and airspeed
next_action.conditions: Bench check with the aircraft powered and no props, no flight.
next_action.baseline: A healthy flight log from the same airframe with live airspeed and yaw-rate values.

outcomes.label: Sensor absent or not logged
outcomes.means: The constant channels and the yaw mismatch are logging or configuration artefacts. No flight fault.
outcomes.then: Close the case as no failure found.

outcomes.label: Sensor fitted but reads zero in a bench test
outcomes.means: There is a real sensor or estimator fault that was present all flight.
outcomes.then: Look at the estimator and sensor health data for the sensor.

unknowns: Why vehicle.attitude[yaw] sits about 30-45 deg from the yaw setpoint all flight (a lag-removed error, so possibly a wrap or offset).
Whether the low-voltage warning at start-up reflects a real battery state, since no battery signal is recorded.

already_answered.question: Did a control fault occur, and when?
already_answered.answer: No onset fault was found. The only startup events are at 0.163 s, and the anomalies line up with commanded setpoint steps.
already_answered.quote: EVENT t=0.163 s controller.event[mavros: Battery] mavros: Battery: WARN: Low voltage

already_answered.question: Did any actuator output freeze or stop following its loop?
already_answered.answer: Outputs 0, 6 and 7 are constant for the whole recording. Outputs 1 and 2 follow throttle. Outputs 3-5 step with the manoeuvres.
already_answered.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[1]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation -0.802 over the recording): it serves that loop

hypotheses.claim: An aileron or elevator output or servo failed or stuck during the 9.7-11.8 s manoeuvre.
hypotheses.because: Outputs 3-5 stepped together and nothing froze at 9.722 s. Measured roll followed the roll setpoint with a normal lag.
hypotheses.observed_at: commanded actuator outputs and attitude estimate

hypotheses.claim: The attitude controller or setpoint source misbehaved, producing the large roll setpoint steps.
hypotheses.because: Roll steps of 27 and 22 deg are in the setpoint and the measured roll follows them. This looks like a commanded manoeuvre, with no mode or failsafe event.

hypotheses.claim: Airspeed and yaw-rate channels are dead and yaw estimate disagrees with its setpoint, from a sensor, estimator or logging issue.
hypotheses.because: Airspeed and yaw rate are constant for the whole recording, yaw error is large throughout, and a sensor-health error appears at start-up.

hypotheses.claim: A low battery or supply fault caused the start-up warnings and affects the sensors.
hypotheses.because: A low-voltage warning appears at 0.163 s, but there is no voltage or current signal and no later brownout sign in the recording.

events.what: Start-up low-voltage warning and sensor-health error
events.why: Boot-time events; they match the dead sensor channels but are not proven to be linked.

events.what: Airspeed and yaw-rate constant at 0 for whole recording
Yaw attitude far from yaw setpoint throughout the flight
events.why: Large steady error, not an onset change.

events.what: Large roll setpoint steps and measured roll response
events.why: Commanded manoeuvres that the aircraft follows.
Throttle manoeuvres alongside the attitude changes.
Unused or fixed channels; no change at any time.

result.lesson: No earlier cases in the workspace, so none apply.
result.reuse_when: A flight shows airspeed and yaw-rate channels constant at zero, a persistent yaw-vs-setpoint offset and a start-up 'Sensor helth' error on a similar MAVROS-based UAV.
